paper_metadata.title: Linformer: Self-Attention with Linear Complexity
paper_metadata.abstract: Large transformer models have shown extraordinary success in achieving state-of-the-art results in many natural language processing applications. However, training and deploying these models can be prohibitively costly for long sequences, as the standard self-attention mechanism of the Transformer uses $O(n^2)$ time and space with respect to sequence length. In this paper, we demonstrate that the self-attention mechanism can be approximated by a low-rank matrix. We further exploit this finding to propose a new self-attention mechanism, which reduces the overall self-attention complexity from $O(n^2)$ to $O(n)$ in both time and space. The resulting linear transformer, the \textit{Linformer}, performs on par with standard Transformer models, while being much more memory- and time-efficient.

extraction_data.innovation: Low-rank approximation of self-attention: decomposes scaled dot-product attention into multiple smaller attention operations through linear projections to form a low-rank factorization, reducing time and space complexity from O(n^2) to O(n) compared to standard quadratic self-attention.
extraction_data.application: Pretrained language modeling, text classification, question answering, translation
extraction_data.research_problem: Reducing the quadratic time and space complexity of self-attention in Transformers for long sequences.
extraction_data.finetuning_task: Supervised fine-tuning on GLUE tasks and sentiment analysis
extraction_data.extension: Adds two linear projection matrices E and F to project keys and values into a k-dimensional space, computing context mapping in O(nk) time and space.
